texts.preamble: Rosy Abraham --/-- vs Ravi Sharma on 3 August, 2023 In The Court Of Harvinder Singh, Presiding Officer : Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-01, (West), Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi. Award/Judgment
texts.facts: Vide this judgment/award, this Tribunal shall decide claim of compensation on account of injuries sustained by injured Rosy Abraham in a road vehicular accident which took place on 23.10.2015 at about 1:10 AM at Tax Barier, Near Prem Dhaba, PS Sadar Rupnagar, Punjab. CASE OF PETITIONER SIDE 2. Succinctly, the case put forward by petition/DAR is that on 23.10.2015 injured Rosy Abraham along with other persons were going on a tour to Manali in a hired Tempo Traveler bearing registration No. DL-1VA-8948 which was being driven by Kamal Garg. At about 1:10 AM, their vehicle reached at Tax Rosy Abraham --/-- vs Ravi Sharma on 3 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189985562/ 3 Barier, Near Prem Dhaba, P.S. Sadar Rupnagar, Punjab. A Truck bearing registration No. HP69A7149 was parked in the middle of the road in rash and negligent manner without any indication or parking lights or reflector in the complete darkness at that place. Due to same, their vehicle bearing registration No. DL1VA8948 struck against said vehicle No. HP69A7149. As a consequence, all the occupants of tempo traveler sustained various injuries. Driver/Kamal Garg and Mrs Maya Abraham died due to same. The incident happened solely due to rash and negligent driving/parking of respondent no.01 who has wrongly parked his vehicle in the middle of the road without any indicators/reflectors. Injured was working as Executive Administration with Sud-Chemie India Pvt. Ltd. And was earning Rs.60,000/- per month at the time of incident. The respondent no.01 being driver, the respondent no.02 being owner and respondent no.03 being the insurer of offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Rosy Abraham Vs. Ravi Sharma & Ors. [MACT No.477648/2016] Page No.4 of 29 HARVINDER SINGH SINGH Date: 2023.08.04 16:47:30 +0530 petitioner(s). The applicant(s)/claimant(s) has/have sought compensation of Rs.22,25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Two Lakhs Twenty Five Thousand Only) from the respondents. MISCELLANEOUS PROCEEDINGS 3. Notice of the application/petition/DAR was issued to the respondents on which they appeared and filed their WS(s)/reply(ies) to the present petition/application. RESPONSE OF RESPONDENT NO.01 &02 4. In gist, the response of the respondent no.01 & 02 as discernible from their reply/written statement is that the respondent no.1 was having a valid driving licence to drive truck bearing registration No. HP69A7149 at the time of incident. Vehicle in question was duly insured with the respondent No.3 covering the date of accident. There was no negligence on the part of the respondent no.1. One set of rear tyres of their vehicle has brusted and its excel has also broken down. Respondent no.1 has parked their vehicle to the left side of the road. Respondent no.1 took all safety measures by giving regular hazardous light. He also put some grass and bricks near the truck so that the other commuters can make out that their vehicle is parked in breakdown condition. Deceased driver of the vehicle bearing no. DL-1VA-8948 was driving at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and hit their vehicle from behind. Incident took place due to the sole negligence of the deceased driver of the vehicle bearing no. DL-1VA-8948. With these averments, respondent no. 1 &2 have prayed for dismissal of the same. RESPONSE OF RESPONDENT NO.03 5. In gist, the response of the respondent no.03 as discernible from its reply/written statement is that Incident in Rosy Abraham Vs. Ravi Sharma & Ors. [MACT No.477648/2016 ] Page No.5 of 29 HARVINDER by HARVINDER SINGH SINGH Date: 2023.08.04 16:47:35 +0530 question took place due to the sole negligence of the deceased who was the driver of vehicle bearing registration No. DL1VA- 8948(Tempo Traveler). Vehicle bearing registration No. HP69A7149 (HGV-Truck) was insured with it vide policy no. 42103/31/15/630002778 for period 03.08.2015 to 02.08.2016 in the name of Sh. Shankar Ram. With these main contentions, respondent No.3 prayed for dismissal of the present petition. ISSUES 6.1 Whether the injured Rosy Abraham suffered injuries in the accident that took place on 22.10.2015 at about 01:10 Am at Tax Barrier, near Prem Dhaba, PS Sadar Rupnagar, Punjab due to rash and negligent driving/parking of vehicle i.e. truck bearing registration number HR69A7149 due to wrongful act or negligence of respondent no.1 Ravi Sharma, who was driving the vehicle? OPP. 2. Whether the petitioner(s)/applicant(s) is/are entitled to compensation, if yes, of what amount and from whom? OPP 3. Relief. 6.2 Thereafter, matter was fixed for evidence of petitioner side. PETITIONER SIDE EVIDENCE 7.1 The petitioner/claimant examined herself as PW1 to establish her claim. She tendered her evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A reiterating and supporting the contents of their application/petition. She relied upon the documents i.e.copy of FIR Mark A, copy of order on charge Mark B, copy of Rosy Abraham Vs. Ravi Sharma & Ors. Date: 2023.08.04 16:47:41 +0530 insurance policy Mark D, copy of DL of driver Mark E, copy of RC Mark F, copy of her Aadhar Card EX.PW1/1 and copy of ITR for the assessment year 2019-20 Ex.PW1/2 in her evidence. PW1 was cross- 7.2 No other witness was examined by petitioner side, petitioner side evidence was closed vide order dated 27.11.2021 and thereafter, matter was fixed for respondent side evidence. RESPONDENT SIDE EVIDENCE 8.1 The respondent no.01 examined himself as R1W1 in connected MACT Petition No. 476356/2016 in case "Santosh vs. Ravi Sharma & ors", and same was ordered to be read in present matter also vide orders dated 02.06.2022. He in gist vide affidavit of evidence Ex.R1W1/A deposed that there was no negligence on his part. He has parked the vehicle on the left side of road and adopted all safely measures like giving regular hazardous light, putting some grass and bricks near the truck so that the other commuters should come to know that the vehicle is parked in breakdown condition. Driver of the vehicle bearing no. DL-1VA-8948 was driving it at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and hit their vehicle in question from behind. R1W1 relied upon the documents i.e. copy of RC Ex.R1W1/1; copy of permit Ex.R1W1/2; copy of his driving license Ex.R1W1/3 and copy of insurance policy Ex.R1W1/4 in his evidence. R1W1 was cross- examined by petitioner side and was discharged. ] Page No.7 of 29 HARVINDER by HARVINDER SINGH SINGH Date: 2023.08.04 16:47:48 +0530 in connected MACT Petition No. 476356/2016 in case Rosy Abraham --/-- vs Ravi Sharma on 3 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189985562/ 5 "Santosh vs. Ravi Sharma & ors" and same was ordered to be read in present matter also vide orders dated 02.06.2022. He in gist vide affidavit of evidence Ex.R2W1/A deposed that there was no negligence on part of respondent no.1. Respondent no.1 parked the vehicle on the left side of road and adopted all safely measures like, giving regular hazardous light, putting some grass and bricks near the truck so that the other commuters should come to know that the vehicle is parked in breakdown condition. Driver of the vehicle bearing no. DL- 1VA-8948 was driving it at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and hit their vehicle in question from behind. R1W1 was cross-examined by petitioner side and was discharged. 8.3 Respondent no.03 examined ASI Khushal Singh of PS City Ropar, District Ropar, Punjab as R3W1 who in gist, has deposed that he was not the IO of the case arising out of FIR No. 112 in question dated 23.10.2015. He was only assisting the IO in the said case. They received information about the accident from the Civil Hospital, Ropar District Roop Nagar, Punjab at around 12:00 noon on 23.10.2015. He accompanied IO ASI Sarabjeet to the Civil Hospital, Ropar where they recorded the statement of Ms. Reena Raju pertaining to the accident. They reached at the spot of accident at about 4:00 PM after getting conducted the post mortem of two deceased/victims of the incident. They found both vehicles in accidental condition. He saw that two rear tyres of the right side of the truck has brusted. The truck was standing on the right side of the road. The Tempo Traveller was strucked Rosy Abraham Vs. Ravi Sharma & Ors. ] Page No.8 of 29 HARVINDER SINGH SINGH Date: 2023.08.04 16:47:54 +0530 beneath the back side of the truck. IO seized both the vehicles. He identified his statements dated 05.08.2016 and 22.02.2017 as Ex. R3W1/1. He also identified the site plan of the place of accident as Ex.R3W1/2 in his evidence. R3W1 was cross- examined, by Ld.Counsel for the petitioner side by Ld. Counsel for respondent no1. & 2 and was discharged. FINAL ARGUMENTS/SUBMISSIONS/CONTENTIONS 9.1 Submissions/contentions of the petitioner side are that the petitioner side has positively proved that the incident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent no.01. The injured was working as Executive Administration with Sud-Chemie India Pvt. Ltd. And was earning Rs.60,000/- per month at the time of incident. She was aged about 53 years at the time of incident. Award may be passed by this Tribunal as per entitlement/claim of applicants/claimants/LRs. 9.2 Submissions/contentions of the respondent no.01 and 02 are that deceased driver of the vehicle bearing no. DL- 1VA-8948 was himself driving his vehicle at a very high speed, in a rash manner and negligent manner. Deceased driver hit their vehicle in question from behind. The petition of the petitioner side may be dismissed. 9.3 Submissions/contentions of the respondent no.03 are that the petitioner/claimant has failed to prove that incident took place due to rash and negligent parking of vehicle in question by respondent no.01. The incident happened due to rash and negligent driving of deceased driver of Tempo Traveler, therefore, they are not liable to pay any compensation to the Rosy Abraham Vs. Ravi Sharma & Ors. on 3 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189985562/ 6 submitted that at least there is contributory negligence on part of deceased driver of Tempo Traveler. texts.arguments: Reference in this regard can be made to the prepositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case of "Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Ors." reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgments in the case of "Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and Ors." 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and "Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors.", 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303 etc. 10.2 10.4 Rule 22 of The Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017 published by Ministry of Road Transport and Highways vide publication no.G.S.R.634(E) dated 23.06.2017 under powers conferred vide Section 118 of M. V. Act, 1988 provides as under : - "22. Stopping and parking.- (1) A vehicle shall not be stopped : - i. at a place where the road is narrow or the view is obstructed; ii. near or on a sharp bend; iii. in an acceleration or a deceleration lane; iv. on, or five meters before, a pedestrian crossing; v. on a level crossing; Rosy Abraham --/-- vs Ravi Sharma on 3 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189985562/ 7 vi. five meters or less before a traffic light signal or "Give Way" sign or "STOP" sign or if a stationary vehicle is likely to obstruct these signs from the view of other road users; vii. at designated bus stands if the vehicle is other than a bus; viii. on a yellow box marked on road; and ix. (2) A vehicle shall not be parked : - (a) at a place where stopping a vehicle is prohibited under sub-regulation (1); (b) on a main road or at a stretch of a road where the notified maximum speed limit is fifty kilometres Rosy Abraham Vs. Ravi Sharma & Ors. 11.2 Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its division bench decision in matter of "Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors." (2011) 1 SCC 343 has held : - "General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 4. The provision of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. (See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467). 5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following : Pecuniary damages (Special Damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. An appropriate multiplier needs to be ascertained as per judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in matter of "Sarla Verma Vs. DTC" 2009 ACJ 1298 SC according to age of the injured/victim.
